title: RobotValues: Evaluating Household Robots When Human Values Conflict
abstract: arXiv:2606.03312v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: While household robots are often evaluated based on task completion, everyday domestic environments involve value-conflicting situations where robots are expected to choose actions that prioritize diverse values such as human autonomy, efficiency, or social appropriateness. Yet, there are no benchmarks for evaluating robots' value preferences in such scenarios. We introduce RobotValues, a benchmark to evaluate household robot planners in 8K value-conflict scenarios. Each instance consists of a realistic, synthetically generated household image with multiple plausible robot actions that prioritize different human values. We construct ROBOTVALUES through LLM-assisted scenario generation, stakeholder-grounded value extraction, image generation and automatic quality control. translated_title: RobotValues：当人类价值观发生冲突时评估家庭机器人
translated_abstract: 虽然家庭机器人通常以任务完成度来评估，但日常家居环境中存在价值冲突的情境，人们期望机器人选择的行动能够优先考虑人类自主性、效率或社会得体性等多样化价值观。然而，目前尚无用于评估机器人在此类情境中价值观偏好的基准。我们提出了RobotValues，一个在8000个价值冲突场景中评估家庭机器人规划器的基准。每个实例由一张真实感的合成家庭场景图像组成，并配有多个合理的机器人行动选项，这些行动分别优先体现不同的人类价值观。我们通过LLM辅助的场景生成、基于利益相关者的价值观提取、图像生成以及自动质量控制来构建RobotValues。我们评估了10个用于机器人领域的视觉语言模型，发现这些模型表现出默认的价值观偏好，包括安全性和顺应性，同时较少选择优先考虑隐私的行动。
tldr: 该论文提出了RobotValues基准，利用8000个价值冲突场景评估家庭机器人规划器的价值观偏好，发现现有视觉语言模型默认偏好安全性和顺应性，而较少选择优先考虑隐私的行动。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RobotValues, a benchmark of 8K value-conflict scenarios for evaluating household robot planners' value preferences, finding that existing VLMs default to safety and accommodation while underselecting privacy-prioritizing actions.
